Title: Password Generator
Description: Generate random passwords of 4–128 characters from uppercase, lowercase, digits and your own symbol set, using the browser's secure RNG.
ErrorNoCharset: Select at least one character set
Keywords: password generator, random password, strong password, secure password generator, custom symbols password, password length 128
Seo_Introduction: Password Generator creates random passwords from the character sets you choose, with a length from 4 to 128 characters. Every character is drawn independently from a cryptographically secure random source inside your browser; nothing is sent anywhere.
Seo_DetailedDescription:
Choose any mix of uppercase A–Z, lowercase a–z, digits 0–9 and special characters. By default the special set is `!@#$%^&*()_+-=[]{}|;:,.<>?` (26 symbols); type your own list in **Custom Symbols** to replace it — duplicates and spaces are dropped so every symbol stays equally likely, and non-ASCII symbols work too. Each position is picked uniformly from the combined alphabet by a Rust/WebAssembly generator seeded from `crypto.getRandomValues`.

A password is generated as soon as the page opens; **Generate Password** creates a new one. The last 10 passwords are listed in **History (last 10)** with their own Copy buttons; the history lives only in the open page and disappears on reload or **Clear History**. Your length and character-set choices are saved in localStorage, the passwords themselves are not.

Strength comes from length and alphabet size: 16 characters from all four default sets (88 symbols) give about 103 bits of entropy. The generator does not force one character from every set, so a short password can occasionally lack a digit or a symbol.
Seo_Examples:
**Everyday account password**: length 16 with all four sets enabled draws from 88 symbols (about 103 bits), producing something like `q7}Rv;2mX!e9Lw@c`.

**Site that allows only a few symbols**: enable **Special Characters** and set **Custom Symbols** to `-_.`; the alphabet becomes 26 + 26 + 10 + 3 = 65 characters, and no other symbol can appear.

**Secret for a .env file**: letters and digits only (62 symbols) at length 64 give about 381 bits, with no quotes or `$` that would need escaping in shell or YAML.

**Numeric test code**: only **Numbers (0-9)** at length 6 gives one of 1,000,000 codes such as `804219` — fine for test data, too weak for an account.
Seo_HowToSteps:
### Step 1: Set the length
Move the **Password Length** slider anywhere from 4 to 128 characters.

### Step 2: Pick character sets
Tick **Uppercase (A-Z)**, **Lowercase (a-z)**, **Numbers (0-9)** and/or **Special Characters**. Optionally list the allowed symbols in **Custom Symbols**.

### Step 3: Generate
Click **Generate Password**. Each click adds the new password to **History (last 10)**.

### Step 4: Copy
Click **Copy** next to the result or next to any entry in the history.
Seo_Tips:
- Length matters more than symbols: each extra character from an 88-symbol alphabet adds about 6.5 bits, while switching symbols on adds less than 0.6 bits per character.
- If a site rejects certain characters, list only the accepted ones in **Custom Symbols** instead of turning special characters off entirely.
- A password without a required digit or symbol is possible for short lengths; just generate again.
- History is kept only in the open tab; use **Clear History** before stepping away from a shared screen.
- Store generated passwords in a password manager; reusing one across sites defeats the randomness.
